Page 5: Document Chunking
Section 1: Document Chunking
Document chunking divides long text into smaller sections.
Each section is called a chunk. Chunking helps the search
system retrieve relevant information efficiently.
Fixed-size chunking uses a defined token limit.
Sentence-based chunking tries to preserve complete sentences.
Recursive character splitting uses separators such as
paragraph breaks, line breaks, and spaces.
Overlapping chunks preserve context between neighboring
sections. A common configuration uses 512 characters
with an overlap of 50 characters.

Semantic search can identify related expressions even
when the query and document use different words.

Technical Document
Document Search Architecture
A document search system processes different file formats.
Text extraction converts PDF and Word documents into plain text.
Text Chunking
Large documents are divided into smaller text chunks.
Each chunk contains a limited number of tokens.
Overlapping chunks help preserve context between sections.
Vector Embeddings
Embedding models convert text into numerical vectors.
Similar meanings produce vectors that are close together.
Search Process
The search system converts user queries into embeddings.
It compares query vectors with stored document vectors.
The most relevant chunks are returned to the user.

sentence_based.text: Technical Document Document Search Architecture A document search system processes different file formats. Text extraction converts PDF and Word documents into plain text. Text Chunking Large documents are divided into smaller text chunks. Each chunk contains a limited number of tokens. Overlapping chunks help preserve context between sections. Vector Embeddings Embedding models convert text into numerical vectors. Similar meanings produce vectors that are close together. Search Process The search system converts user queries into embeddings. It compares query vectors with stored document vectors. The most relevant chunks are returned to the user.

cosine similarity. Embeddings are stored alongside

Product Guide

Our software provides document search functionality.
Users can upload PDF, DOCX, and TXT files.
The system converts documents into text before processing.
Text is divided into smaller chunks.
Embeddings represent the meaning of each chunk.
Semantic search retrieves relevant information based on meaning.

Technical Document
Document Search Architecture
A document search system processes different file formats.
Text extraction converts PDF and Word documents into plain text.
Text Chunking
Large documents are divided into smaller text chunks.
Each chunk contains a limited number of tokens.
Overlapping chunks help preserve context between sections.
Vector Embeddings
Embedding models convert text into numerical vectors.
Similar meanings produce vectors that are close together.

Search Process
The search system converts user queries into embeddings.
It compares query vectors with stored document vectors.
The most relevant chunks are returned to the user.

Introduction
This manual introduces employees to the document search system.
Document Upload
Users can upload PDF, Word, and text documents. The system extracts text from each document.
Chunking Process
Documents are divided into smaller chunks. Each chunk stores metadata such as source, page, and chunk index.
Search Process
The system uses embeddings to identify relevant information. Users receive the most relevant document sections.
